key_insight: The paper introduces ergoCub, a humanoid robot designed to be safer for humans by jointly optimizing hardware and motion for both locomotion and human-aware metrics like spinal load. In simple terms, it shows that robot performance and human safety can be improved together rather than traded off.
problem_solved: Humanoid robots often optimize for speed, balance, or task success without accounting for the physical burden they may place on nearby humans or operators. This work addresses the need for human-aware design and control that reduces biomechanical risk while preserving robust walking.
method: Uses a shared embodied intelligence framework to co-optimize robot design and control.
Includes human-related objectives, such as back stress/spinal load, alongside locomotion performance metrics.
Tests the resulting ergoCub platform to evaluate safety-oriented design choices and walking robustness.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights a practical path toward embodied AI systems that are not only capable but also ergonomically and physically considerate. It is especially relevant for robotics, human-robot interaction, and safety-critical deployment settings.
visual_elements: Split-system diagram showing joint optimization of hardware design and locomotion control
Before/after comparison of spinal load or back-stress metrics
Humanoid robot silhouette with highlighted human-safety pressure or force zones
Performance trade-off chart balancing walking robustness vs. human-aware safety metrics
paper_title: Towards shared embodied intelligence in humanoid robots through optimization, development and testing of the human-aware ergoCub robot
paper_authors: Carlotta Sartore, Mohamed Elobaid, Lorenzo Rapetti, Giulio Romualdi, Stefano Dafarra
